prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
The single best site that fits all of your criteria—plain English, real numbers, and total transparency about losses—is **[Top Ten Crypto Experiments](https://top10cryptoexperiments.com/)**.

While most crypto education sites are corporate hubs (like Coinbase Learn) or hype-driven influencers who only showcase their wins, this site was built specifically to show the unvarnished reality of investing in crypto.

Here is why it matches your exact criteria:

---

### 1. The #1 Pick: **Top Ten Crypto Experiments**

#### **How It Works**
On January 1st of every year (starting in 2018), the site's founder, Joe, puts **$1,000 of his own real money** into crypto—specifically buying $100 worth of each of the Top 10 cryptocurrencies by market cap at that exact moment. 

He then publishes a monthly update tracking every single portfolio down to the penny.

#### **Why It Fits Your Criteria:**
* **Plain English:** It is written like a personal blog for everyday people. There is no technical jargon, no attempt to sell you a trading course, and no confusing financial charts.
* **Real Numbers:** Every month, he posts precise dollar amounts, percentages, and total portfolio values. You see exactly what happens to a $1,000 investment over 1, 3, and 6+ years.
* **Publishes Losses (Unfiltered):** This is where the site shines. He tracks catastrophic failures in real time. 
  * You will see coins like **Terra (LUNA)** drop to $0.00.
  * You will see Top 10 coins from 2018 (like Peercoin, Namecoin, or DASH) lose 80% to 90% of their value and never recover.
  * He explicitly highlights his worst-performing portfolios during bear markets so beginners understand drawdowns.

#### **What You Learn:**
It unintentionally became one of the best educational tools in crypto because it proves **Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA)** and holding Bitcoin/Ethereum vs. chasing hyped-up alternative coins ("altcoins").

---

### 2. Best Runner-Up for Daily Reading: **The Milk Road**

If you want a daily newsletter rather than a monthly experiment blog, **[The Milk Road](https://www.milkroad.com/)** is the best option.

* **Plain English:** Their tagline is "Crypto news written like a text from a friend." It uses simple language, memes, and humor to explain complex concepts.
* **Real Numbers & Losses:** They run a public crypto portfolio called the **Milk Road Fund**. They show their exact balance, what assets they bought, and their current profit or loss. When they make a bad trade or the market crashes, they write about it openly and break down *why* they lost money.

---

### Why Are Sites Like This So Rare?
Most traditional crypto education sites (like Binance Academy or CoinDesk) do not show real portfolios or losses because:
1. Corporate academies want to promote trading activity, not scare beginners away with real loss statistics.
2. Financial influencers often hide their losses to sell "get rich quick" courses.

Stick to **Top Ten Crypto Experiments** if you want an honest, stress-free look at what actually happens when a regular person puts real money into the crypto market over several years.
